members.working:
Determine the nature (diamagnetic or paramagnetic) of the product containing the named element for each reaction.
(i) SO₂ with K₂Cr₂O₇ in acid medium reduces Cr(VI) to Cr(III). Cr³⁺ has d³ configuration (unpaired electrons) → paramagnetic, not diamagnetic.
(ii) FeS₂ roasted in excess air oxidizes sulfur; iron likely forms Fe₂O₃ or Fe₃O₄, both contain Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ with unpaired electrons → paramagnetic.
(iii) C with Al₂O₃ and N₂ at high temperature typically produces graphite or possibly diamond; both forms of carbon have all electrons paired → diamagnetic.
(iv) CuSO₄ with excess KI reduces Cu(II) to Cu(I) (CuI precipitate). Cu(I) d¹⁰ configuration has no unpaired electrons → diamagnetic.
(v) Cu(OH)₂ on heating decomposes to CuO (black). Cu²⁺ d⁹ configuration has one unpaired electron → paramagnetic.
Thus reactions (iii) and (iv) give diamagnetic products. Number of such reactions = 2.

members.working:
Identify product containing named element for each reaction and determine hybridisation of that element in the product.
(i) CoCl₃ + NH₃ → Co(III) complex with NH₃ ligands; Co in octahedral complex, typically sp³ hybridised (four-coordinate? Actually Co(III) with NH₃ often d⁶ low-spin, geometry octahedral, hybridisation sp³? In complexes, hybridisation concept less strict; but typical description: Co in complex uses sp³ hybridisation for bonding to ligands. So sp³.
(ii) P₄S₁₀ hydrolysis → P₄O₁₀ or H₃PO₄? Product containing P likely P₄O₁₀ or H₃PO₄; phosphorus in phosphate is tetrahedral (sp³). So sp³.
(iii) CO + Cl₂ under sunlight/catalyst → phosgene? Actually CO + Cl₂ → CCl₂? Known reaction: CO + Cl₂ → COCl₂ (phosgene) under light; C in COCl₂ is trigonal planar (sp²). So not sp³.
(iv) N₂ + H₂ with Fe catalyst at high T → ammonia NH₃; N in NH₃ is sp³ (trigonal pyramidal). So sp³.
(v) H₂ + O₂ ignition → H₂O; O in H₂O is sp³ (bent). So sp³.
(vi) [Ag(CN)₂]⁻ + Zn → Zn metal or Zn complex? In cyanide process, Zn reduces Ag⁺ to metallic Ag, Zn goes to Zn²⁺ in solution; product containing Zn likely Zn²⁺ aqua complex, tetrahedral/square planar, often sp³ hybridised. So sp³.
Thus reactions with sp³: (i),(ii),(iv),(v),(vi) = 5. (iii) is sp².
Answer integer 5.
